sections.heading: What the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 promised

blocks.text: The **AP Reorganisation Act, 2014** (effective **2 June 2014**) carried a compensation package for the residual state that lost its capital and revenue engine. The promises fall into six baskets — and their fulfilment scorecard is the single most asked AP-economy question.

rows: PM's assurance on the **Rajya Sabha floor (20 Feb 2014)** — not in the Act itself
**Not granted**; Centre offered a 'special package' (2016) of equivalent assistance instead; 14th FC's dropping of the SCS category cited — the running political-fiscal dispute
**Sec 46**: standardised support for the first year's resource gap
Partially paid; AP claims a large unpaid balance (thousands of crores) based on CAG-audited gap vs Centre's assessed figure — a live Centre-state accounting dispute
**Sec 90**: declared national project; Centre to execute & fund

Centre funds via PPA; cost-revision disputes (2013-14 price level vs revised estimates), R&R funding gaps, diaphragm-wall damage; commissioning repeatedly rescheduled — partially fulfilled, heavily delayed
IIT Tirupati, IIM Visakhapatnam, NIT (Tadepalligudem), IIIT Kurnool, Central University (Anantapur), IISER Tirupati, AIIMS Mangalagiri, agri & petroleum universities, tribal university
Largely **delivered** — most established and functioning (some on transit campuses for years); Vizag railway zone (**South Coast Railway**) sanctioned 2019, operationalisation dragged
Sec 94: tax incentives; special development package for **7 backward districts of Rayalaseema + north-coastal AP** (₹50 cr/district/year pattern)
Partially paid; AP claims arrears; incentives modest relative to the Hyderabad-loss scale
Sec 93/Schedule: metro rail examinations, ports (Duggirajupatnam), refinery/petrochemicals (Kakinada zone), airports
Mixed: some examined and dropped as unviable, others (petro corridor) slow — the weakest basket

sections.heading: Central assistance and the conflict — both sides

items: **AP's case**: bifurcation was imposed without consent (Assembly resolution rejected); the state lost ~45% of revenue with 58% of population; assurances (SCS, deficit funding) were the consideration for acquiescence — non-fulfilment is breach of a federal compact; per-capita income fell below neighbours'.

**Centre's case**: SCS category ended with plan abolition/14th FC architecture; equivalent assistance offered via EAP-route special package; revenue-gap arithmetic disputed; Polavaram funded but cost inflation needs scrutiny; many Schedule-13 items delivered.

**The federal lesson**: statutory promises fared better than floor assurances — institutions (in the Act) came; SCS (a speech) did not. For GS answers this is the textbook case for **codifying reorganisation packages** and for a **neutral arbitration mechanism** for Centre-state financial disputes (Punchhi's suggestion of institutionalised intergovernmental councils).

**Current turn**: post-2024, with the state's party pivotal at the Centre, budgets earmarked **special support for AP** — capital (Amaravati ~₹15,000 crore via multilateral windows), Polavaram funding reaffirmed, backward-region funds — pragmatic accommodation replacing the SCS demand without conceding it.

sections.heading: 💰 Deep mastery — the Reorganisation Act promises, tracked

items: **The 13th Schedule commitments:** national institutions — **IIT Tirupati, IIM Visakhapatnam, NIT AP (Tadepalligudem), Central University (Anantapur), IIIT, AIIMS Mangalagiri, IISER Tirupati, NIDM, Central Institute** — largely established, though with funding and campus delays.

**Big-ticket promises & the conflict:** **Special Category Status** (assured on the RS floor, 2014; denied after the 14th FC, offered a 'special package' instead), **revenue-deficit grant**, **Polavaram** (declared a national project — reimbursement disputes over the ₹ component and irrigation vs drinking-water cost split), and backward-district support for **Rayalaseema & north-coastal AP**.
**The capital question:** the Act left AP without a capital; the Amaravati greenfield-capital effort and central support for a new capital remain contested and under-resourced.
**Verdict:** partial fulfilment; the SCS and Polavaram funding gaps are the sharpest Union–State grievances — the model 'trust-deficit' case study for Paper-III federalism too.

sections.heading: AP's public debt — the load-bearing wall

blocks.text: AP's **outstanding liabilities** are around **one-third of GSDP** (roughly ₹4.5–5 lakh crore scale in recent years) — among the higher ratios for large states — with CAG flagging **additional off-budget borrowings via state corporations and guarantees** that push the effective burden higher. Composition: market borrowings (SDLs) dominate, plus NSSF, central loans (incl. capex-loan window), and **external debt** (multilateral, back-to-back through the Centre). Consequences: **interest payments absorb a heavy share of revenue receipts** (high double digits %), crowding capex; the state's fiscal strategy is therefore inseparable from its debt strategy.

rows: **World Bank + ADB (~$800 mn each, ~₹15,000 cr programme)**
Trunk infrastructure of the capital — the flagship EAP
Kurnool/NP Kunta ultra-mega solar parks ecosystem

blocks.text: EAPs are **cheaper and longer-tenor** than SDLs but **project-tied, conditionality-bearing and slow-disbursing** — an evaluation line examiners reward.

sections.heading: Mineral and forest resources — the endowment ledger

items: **Minerals**: AP is a top-tier mineral state — India's leading producer of **barytes (Mangampeta, Kadapa — among the world's largest deposits)**, **mica (Gudur, Nellore — historic belt)**, major **limestone** reserves (cement belt of Kadapa-Kurnool-Guntur-Krishna), **laterite/bauxite** (Eastern Ghats — extraction contested on tribal/Fifth Schedule grounds), **manganese** (Vizianagaram-Srikakulam), **beach sands** (ilmenite/monazite — regulated, atomic minerals), **granite** (Ongole/Chimakurthy black galaxy), plus **oil & gas in the KG Basin** (onshore + offshore; KG-D6 era finds). Revenue instruments: royalties, **DMF (District Mineral Foundation)** funds for mining-affected areas, auction premia post-MMDR 2015.

**Forests**: ~**37,000+ sq km recorded forest area (~23% of geography)**; Eastern Ghats deciduous belts, **red sanders** (endemic to Seshachalam — CITES-listed, smuggling-prone), bamboo, tendu, NTFP sustaining tribal livelihoods (GCC — Girijan Cooperative Corporation monopoly procurement); mangroves at **Coringa** (2nd largest mangrove system on the east coast after Sundarbans). Revenue is modest; the real economics is **ecosystem services + NTFP livelihoods + eco-tourism**, constrained by conservation law (FCA, Wildlife Act, **Forest Rights Act 2006** recognition backlog).

**The governance tension**: mineral wealth sits under **Fifth Schedule tribal land** (bauxite in Visakhapatnam agency) — **Samatha v. State of AP (1997)**: government land in scheduled areas cannot be leased to private mining companies; the judgment is AP's gift to national tribal-rights jurisprudence and a mandatory citation.

**Resource-mobilisation verdict**: minerals and forests are **supplementary, not transformative**, revenue (single-digit % of receipts) — their real value is industrial feedstock (cement, pharma-limestone, gas for fertiliser/power) and livelihood security; over-extraction risks the Samatha-PESA-FRA legal wall and ecological costs.

sections.heading: 💰 Deep mastery — debt sustainability & the resource endowment

items: **Debt sustainability test (Domar):** debt is sustainable if the nominal growth rate exceeds the effective interest rate (**g > r**); AP's rising **debt-to-GSDP** ratio and off-budget liabilities have drawn CAG and RBI-State-Finances scrutiny.

**The mineral ledger:** AP is rich in **limestone, barytes (Mangampet — among the world's largest deposits), heavy mineral beach sands (ilmenite, garnet, monazite), mica, dolomite, and granite/quartz**; coastal AP hosts oil & gas (KG basin).
**Forest & bio-resources:** Eastern Ghats forests, the Nallamala and agency areas — biodiversity and NTFP wealth, but also the tension of mining vs Fifth-Schedule tribal rights (FRA 2006).

**Way forward:** monetise mineral wealth transparently (District Mineral Foundation funds for local development), control off-budget borrowing, and improve capital-expenditure quality to grow out of the debt trap.

sections.heading: Why water is AP's existential resource question

blocks.text: AP is a **lower riparian** on both its lifelines — **Krishna** and **Godavari** — making inter-state water relations the state's most consequential resource dispute. The constitutional frame: **water is a State subject (Entry 17, List II)** subject to **Entry 56, List I** (inter-state rivers); **Art 262** + the **Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956** route disputes to tribunals and **bar Supreme Court jurisdiction** over tribunal awards (though Art 136/32 petitions have crept back in practice).

rows: Maharashtra, Karnataka, (undivided) AP → now AP & Telangana; **KWDT-I (Bachawat, 1976)**: 811 TMC to undivided AP at 75% dependability; **KWDT-II (Brijesh Kumar, 2010/13)** allocations **not yet notified** (SC stay)

Post-2014: **AP-Telangana sharing** of the undivided 811 TMC (operating ad-hoc ~66:34); Telangana seeks fresh allocation; **Sec 89** reference to KWDT-II for project-wise allocation between the two; escalations over Srisailam-Nagarjunasagar operations

Less conflictual (surplus river); issues: Polavaram backwater objections (Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Telangana), Telangana's upstream projects (Kaleshwaram) and AP's counter-claims on surplus-water diversions (Banakacherla proposal controversy)
**KRMB & GRMB** created by the **Reorganisation Act (Secs 85–87)**; jurisdiction over notified projects gazetted **2021**
Implementation friction: handing over projects, telemetry, unapproved projects lists — the institutional battleground

sections.heading: The deeper anatomy — and the way forward

items: **Why disputes persist**: tribunal delays (KWDT-II two decades unresolved), non-notification of awards, **hydrological change vs fixed allocations** (dependability assumptions age badly under climate volatility), upstream storage races, election-cycle escalation, and data distrust (telemetry gaps).

**AP's specific stakes**: Krishna delta and Rayalaseema drought belt both depend on assured releases; **Srisailam** (power vs irrigation trade-off with Telangana), **Rayalaseema lift schemes** vs Telangana's Palamuru-Rangareddy — mirror-image grievances; Polavaram as the Godavari game-changer (its Krishna-basin transfer of 80 TMC releases equivalent Krishna water upstream — the inter-basin bargain of the 1978 GWDT agreements).

**Reform menu**: notify KWDT-II/complete the Sec-89 exercise; empower KRMB/GRMB with full project control + real-time telemetry; a permanent tribunal with time-limits (the **Inter-State River Water Disputes (Amendment) Bill** — single standing tribunal, DRC first — pending); basin-level authorities (the River Basin Management Bill idea); demand-side: micro-irrigation, crop-shifting in delta paddy, groundwater recharge (AP's tank-restoration legacy — Neeru-Chettu era works).

**Balanced close**: water disputes are **federal relations under scarcity** — the durable solution is institutional (standing tribunal + basin authority + telemetry transparency) plus hydrological (augmentation via Polavaram/inter-basin transfers) plus demand management; litigation alone allocates grievance, not water.

sections.heading: 💰 Deep mastery — water as AP's binding constraint

items: **The two lifelines:** the **Godavari** (surplus, less contested) and the **Krishna** (deficit, fiercely contested) — AP is a lower-riparian, so **KWDT-I (Bachawat, 1976)** and **KWDT-II (Brijesh Kumar)** allocations are existential.

**The AP–Telangana dispute:** post-2014 sharing of Krishna waters, the roles of the **Krishna & Godavari River Management Boards** (jurisdiction notified 2021), and projects like **Rayalaseema Lift, Pothireddypadu, Kaleshwaram (TS)** keep the dispute live before the tribunal and courts.

**Irrigation & drought:** Rayalaseema's chronic drought vs the deltaic surplus; **Polavaram** (Godavari) to divert water to the Krishna delta and Rayalaseema is the keystone project; micro-irrigation (drip/sprinkler) and the **Godavari–Cauvery interlinking** proposal are the demand-side answers.
**Way forward:** finish Polavaram, honour tribunal awards, invest in watershed/rainwater harvesting and drip irrigation, and depoliticise inter-state water governance.
